idiom_name: unexported struct with injected dependencies + consumer-side interfaces; package-level functions when there is nothing to inject
implementation_notes: The idiomatic Go service is a small struct in the domain package holding its collaborators (type FundsTransfer struct { accounts AccountRepository; clock Clock }) with a NewFundsTransfer constructor, while the port interfaces are declared where they are consumed ('accept interfaces, return structs') so the domain package imports no infrastructure. When the operation needs no collaborators, a package-level function is enough and the struct is noise - that function is the replacement for the classic service object. Go cannot enforce statelessness, so keeping the fields unexported and set once in the constructor is the discipline that makes the service safe to share across goroutines.
pitfalls: Storing per-request data (a transaction handle, the calling user, an *http.Request) in the service struct turns it into shared mutable state; pass per-request values as parameters and reserve context.Context for cancellation, deadlines and request-scoped values used by application code.

Declaring the interface next to its implementation ('provider side') defeats the inversion: declare the port in the consuming domain package so the implementation can be swapped and the import direction stays inward.
A nil receiver or a nil dependency fails only when the method runs; validate injected collaborators in the constructor so tests and wiring mistakes surface at startup.
